subject: Finexus - Post-incident executive summary and remediation evidence
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@finexus.com>, support@finexus.com
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Finexus - interim incident summary and next steps

Elaine / Finexus team,

Thank you again for taking the call earlier. I wanted to follow up with an interim summary of what we know so far and the near-term actions Redwood will take. We'll share the complete RCA and evidence bundle once our SRE analysis completes (target: Friday PST).

What happened (interim):
- Between 11/29 22:10 UTC and 11/29 22:42 UTC Finexus saw a spike in dropped tokens and partial outputs from our hosted inference path when your traffic changed to longer sequences and a higher fraction of streaming calls.
- Our automatic fallback routing triggered to a lower-capacity model variant for ~25 minutes while autoscaling adjusted, which led to increased token latency and several incomplete responses for session-affine workloads.

Immediate actions we're taking:
1) Full export of the request timeline and kernel metrics (attached as finexus-rca-timeline.csv).
2) SRE-led investigation into cache eviction thresholds and routing policy mismatches (Rafael leading).
3) Short-term mitigation: pinning your routing policy to the dedicated pool and increasing KV cache retention for your account (ASAP; applied 11/30 18:00 PST).

What we need from you:
- A quick confirmation that applying the pinned routing policy is acceptable for the next 72 hours while we validate fixes.

We know this disrupted your surface area and apologize for the impact. Rafael will share a detailed timeline and the root-cause hypothesis in the next message.

Regards,

Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: finexus-rca-timeline.csv

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 02:28:00 -0800
Subject: Finexus - technical RCA and timeline (attached evidence)

Elaine / Aditya,

Thanks for the prompt escalation. Below is the SRE team's consolidated technical timeline, root cause, and the short/medium-term mitigations we've already applied or will complete by next week. I've attached the timeline CSV and an architecture diagram that highlights where the mismatch occurred (kv-cache-rca-diagram.png). Full evidence bundle is in postmortem-evidence.zip on the Drive link shared in the metadata.

Summary timeline (UTC):
- 2027-11-29 22:05 — Finexus traffic changes: 40% increase in avg sequence length (streaming + echo requests).
- 2027-11-29 22:10 — Autonomous batching reconfiguration triggered due to longer sequences; concurrent KV cache pressure rose.
- 2027-11-29 22:12 — Cache evictions began for some session-affine keys when retention crossed eviction threshold.
- 2027-11-29 22:18 — Smart routing logic determined fallback to a lower-memory model variant for a subset of requests to maintain tail-latency SLOs.
- 2027-11-29 22:42 — Autoscaler completed capacity add; routing reverted and normal behavior resumed.

Root cause (concise):
- Interaction between (a) our dynamic batching/autoscaling logic and (b) conservative KV cache eviction thresholds for shared hosting pools. Under the changed workload, the system favored preserving tail latency by shifting some sessions to a smaller model variant. That shift did not preserve session KV affinity for a subset of streaming calls, resulting in partial outputs and token truncation.

Impact:
- Window: ~22 minutes; affected ~2.7% of Finexus inference calls during the spike (~1,200 calls with partial outputs).
- No data exfiltration or unauthorized access observed. No persisted customer data lost; retries occurred at the application layer (Finexus reported some duplicate downstream events).

Short-term mitigations completed (applied 2027-11-30):
- Pinned Finexus routing to your dedicated pool for 72 hours (reduces likelihood of cross-tenant cache pressure).
- Increased KV cache retention ceiling for your tenant by 2x to avoid transient evictions during bursts.
- Adjusted fallback policy so streaming calls prefer model variants that maintain session-affinity.

Medium-term fixes (in progress, ETA 2027-12-08):
- Permanent change to routing policy precedence to consider session affinity before variant fallback.
- Autoscaler tuning to stage capacity adds earlier when average sequence length rises above threshold.
- Add a pre-flight estimation that simulates batch memory before committing to variant fallback.

Action items and owners: (JIRA:INC-4871)
- Rafael Mendes: Postmortem writeup and evidence upload (done - Drive link)
- Hannah Schmitt: Implement routing precedence change (in progress, PR opened)
- Marissa Cole: Coordinate customer verification window and credit request (CS lead)
- Aditya Rao: Final customer-facing RCA and executive summary (today)

Attachments: finexus-rca-timeline.csv, kv-cache-rca-diagram.png

If helpful, we can run a validation window with Finexus traffic replay this week to demonstrate the fix under controlled load.

— Rafael Mendes
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ra.fael@redwood.ai (mobile redacted)

Elaine,

Thanks for the fast collaboration. A few practical items to close the loop:

1) Verification window — Redwood will run a controlled 4-hour verification during your low-volume window on 12/03 (00:00 - 04:00 UTC). Rafael's team will provide live metrics and a short play-by-play. Please confirm a contact for the run.

2) Compensation — We're offering a billing credit equivalent to one week of hosted inference usage for the Finexus account, applied to your next invoice. We'll also cover one engineering validation replay if you want Redwood to run it end-to-end.

3) Executive RCA — Aditya will send the customer-facing one-page RCA (with timeline and action owners) and the Drive evidence link; Rafael's technical appendix is attached.

Please reply with the verification contact and approval for the credit; once we have that we'll schedule the replay and mark the incident closed on our side after successful verification.

Warm regards,

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
